Coinkite shipped emergency firmware on July 31, but it cannot repair an existing seed, so owners with exposed devices must generate a new seed and move their coins.

title: Coldcard Thefts Near $114 Million as Fourth Attack Wave Hits
blurb: Attackers launched a fourth wave of sweeps against Coldcard hardware wallets on Monday, pushing estimated losses to roughly 1,816 BTC, or about $114 million, since Thursday. The thefts trace to a firmware bug that shipped in March 2021 and undercut hardware wallets' core promise that on-device keys cannot be guessed, prompting maker Coinkite to release emergency firmware and halt shipments.

title: Hackers Poison Adform Script to Swap Crypto Wallet Addresses Across Customer Sites
blurb: Attackers compromised a JavaScript file served by ad-tech firm Adform, injecting code that rewrote copied and typed Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tron wallet addresses to redirect payments to attacker-controlled destinations. Because the poisoned trackpoint-async.js loads across many unrelated client sites, the incident is a supply-chain compromise; Adform detected it on July 27, removed the code, and is telling users to clear cached scripts and verify any address before sending funds.

title: Bitcoin Bridge Boltz Halts Swaps Indefinitely, Citing AI-Assisted Attacks
blurb: Boltz, the non-custodial bridge routing swaps between Bitcoin mainchain, Lightning and Liquid, disabled its service indefinitely on Aug. 3, citing months of automated, AI-assisted attacks that outpaced its ability to patch. The bootstrapped team said contained exploits cost the company money but never put user funds at risk given its atomic-swap design, and cut off swap rails behind wallets including Bull Bitcoin and Aqua.

title: Kalshi and Polymarket’s combined volume reaches all-time high in July, surpassing $50 billion
blurb: Kalshi and Polymarket's combined trading volume topped $50B in July, an all-time monthly high for prediction markets. Polymarket US grew 54% month-over-month while the main Polymarket platform fell 26%, signaling that the CFTC-regulated US venue is absorbing demand as offshore volume cools.

title: DEX Spot Volume Hit a Record 24% of CEX Volume in July
blurb: DEX spot volume reached 24.14% of centralized exchange volume in July, the highest ratio since The Block's data series began in 2019. The record share came in a shrinking market, as onchain volume held up better than CEX volume even while both fell and DEX spot totals dropped 26% to $130.77 billion, the lowest monthly figure since September 2024.

title: The $114 Trillion Question: How DTCC Is Tokenizing the Entire U.S. Market
blurb: DTCC, the clearinghouse that settles $114 trillion in US securities, demonstrated on July 15 that it can tokenize those assets, trade them in live production conditions, and convert them back without disrupting existing settlement rails. The pilot signals that the largest pool of traditional financial assets could move onchain through incumbent infrastructure rather than crypto-native venues.

title: RWAs Topped Half of Hyperliquid's Volume for Two Straight Weeks in July
blurb: RWA perps topped half of Hyperliquid's trading volume for two straight weeks in July, doing $25.1B, or 52%, of the platform's $48.2B total in the week of July 13–19, the first time stock, commodity and index perps out-traded crypto pairs. The RWA category, run on the HIP-3 framework, is masking a shrinking crypto perps business as quarterly volume fell from a ~$1T Q3 2025 peak to about $550B in Q2 2026.

title: SEC keeps Nasdaq bitcoin options on hold after granting CME review
blurb: CME Group petitioned the SEC to overturn a staff decision that conditionally approved Nasdaq PHLX's proposal to list cash-settled bitcoin index options, arguing the contracts are commodity option swaps under the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction. The SEC granted the review and kept the approval stayed pending written statements due Aug. 24, leaving Nasdaq's index-referenced contracts blocked over the same securities-versus-commodity question that separates them from existing spot-ETF options.

title: Saylor hints at Strategy bitcoin buy after five-week pause as STRC rate stays at 12%: ‘Bitcoin Drive engaged’
blurb: Michael Saylor captioned Strategy's Sunday chart post "Bitcoin Drive engaged," signaling the firm may disclose its first bitcoin purchase in five weeks after an atypical drought that saw it instead sell shares, lift its dollar reserve to $3.75 billion, and buy back STRC. Strategy last reported holding 843,775 BTC acquired for $63.69 billion, and separately said it will keep STRC's variable annualized dividend rate at 12% for August.

title: SummerFi to Wind Down After Seven Years, Citing Exploit
blurb: SummerFi will wind down Summer.fi and sunset its user interface after seven years, attributing the decision to a recent exploit on its Lazy Summer Protocol that drained roughly $6M. The operator has not set a wind-down date or clarified the status of user funds, and its closure follows Zapper's planned Aug. 3 shutdown as DeFi front ends buckle under security and operating costs.

title: Proof of Attendance Protocol is shutting down after 5+ years
blurb: Proof of Attendance Protocol is winding down after more than five years, co-founder Isabel Gonzalez announced, ending a project that minted millions of onchain event badges for 46,210 issuers including Coinbase, American Express, and Bayer. Gonzalez cited crypto's funding cycles and distribution dynamics, joining a wave of culturally established projects like Leap Wallet, Zapper, and BitMEX that have shut down amid tight capital conditions.

title: BlackRock launches two tokenized money market funds for stablecoin reserves
blurb: BlackRock launched two tokenized money market products, BRSRV, a new fund built for stablecoin issuers to park reserves and earn yield, and BSTBL, a tokenized share class of an existing Treasury liquidity fund. The push extends BlackRock's onchain footprint beyond BUIDL, which holds over $2.6B in assets, as tokenized US Treasuries have grown from $721M to $16B since March 2024.

title: Tornado Cash Logs 968 Deposits in Busiest Day of 2026, L2Beat Says
blurb: Tornado Cash processed 968 deposits on July 23, its busiest day of 2026, with the Drift exploiter contributing 78% via 23,095 ETH.

title: Michael Saylor says he’s never sold his personal bitcoin after Strategy dumps more BTC
blurb: Saylor says he's never sold any personal bitcoin, after Strategy disclosed selling 1,638 BTC for $104.7M last week.

title: Crypto Card Volume Hits $748.7M in July, a Fifth Straight Monthly Gain: Paymentscan
blurb: Crypto payment card spending hit a record $748.7M in July, up 19.1% from June and 144.7% year-over-year, marking a fifth straight monthly all-time high across roughly 20 chains tracked by Paymentscan. RedotPay processed $395.1M, more than half of tracked volume, as stablecoin-funded cards keep setting usage records even while trading volumes fall to multi-year lows.

title: Jameson Lopp says Coldcard exploit exposes limits of Bitcoin’s ‘don’t trust, verify’ mantra
blurb: An ongoing Coldcard exploit has drained over 1,300 BTC (~$83M) from thousands of self-custody addresses across multiple waves, stemming from a 2021 seed-generation bug that reduced entropy and let attackers brute-force affected wallets remotely. Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp argues the incident exposes the limits of "don't trust, verify," since verifying complex hardware and software is infeasible for nearly all users, who inevitably trust vendors, developers, and researchers instead.

title: Strategy Sells 1,638 Bitcoin for $105M, Splits Proceeds Between Dividends and STRC Buyback
blurb: Strategy sold 1,638 bitcoin for $104.73 million between July 27 and Aug. 2, splitting the proceeds evenly to cover $52.4 million in preferred stock dividends and $52.3 million in STRC share buybacks. The sale, part of the BTC Monetization Program launched in late June, priced coins about 15% below their cost basis and leaves the company holding 842,138 bitcoin against a 12.00% STRC dividend it must keep servicing.

title: Flap Overtakes Pump.fun in Daily Revenue With $1.18 Million
blurb: Flap, a BNB Chain token launchpad, generated $1.18M in revenue on Aug. 1, edging out the $1.1M earned across the entire Pump.fun family for the first time, per DefiLlama. The BNB Chain flip is narrow and recent, with Pump still dominant over longer windows at $31.4M in 30-day revenue against Flap's $4.42M and over $1B in lifetime launchpad fees.

title: 'I Did Everything Right': Coldcard Victims Recount Losing Life Savings
blurb: A firmware bug in Coldcard hardware wallets made generated seeds guessable, letting attackers reproduce private keys and sweep roughly 1,816 BTC, worth about $114 million, from more than 5,200 addresses across four coordinated waves. Victims who followed the self-custody playbook, storing offline-generated seeds in safes and safety deposit boxes, are now racing to move remaining coins before attackers reach them first.

title: Trump Media’s bitcoin stash may be down to loan collateral after $165 million BTC move
blurb: Trump Media moved 2,628 bitcoin worth about $165 million to Crypto.com, leaving roughly 4,261 BTC in tagged wallets that closely match the amount pledged as collateral for its convertible notes. On-chain analysts estimate the company's bitcoin bets, made near last cycle's top for $1.37 billion, have produced about $318 million in realized losses, with its Q2 10-Q the test of whether recent transfers were sales or custody moves.

title: FalconX Cuts Staff on Extended Downturn in Crypto Markets
blurb: FalconX cut 10% of its global staff, positioning the digital-asset brokerage for a prolonged crypto market downturn, according to people familiar with the matter. The reduction at one of the sector's largest institutional prime brokers signals thinning trading volumes and tighter margins across the crypto brokerage business heading into the second half of 2026.

title: Marc Andreessen & Chris Dixon: Why America needs CLARITY
blurb: Marc Andreessen and Chris Dixon made the case for the CLARITY Act on a new podcast, arguing the crypto market structure bill now moving through the Senate is once-in-a-generation legislation that will determine where the financial system gets built. The bill passed the House last year with bipartisan support, and the pair contend that leaving the sector without clear rules is the costlier path for the US.

title: Trump-backed American Bitcoin posts $57m loss but grows its BTC treasury
blurb: American Bitcoin, the Trump-family-backed miner majority owned by Hut 8, narrowed its Q2 net loss to $57.2m from $81.8m the prior quarter while lifting its treasury 14% to 8,002 bitcoin. Mining revenue rose 8% to $67m on record production of 932 coins, but the mine-and-hold strategy leaves the first half of 2026 more than $139m in the red.

title: Senators Urge CFTC to Curb Wildfire Prediction Market Bets Over Arson Concerns
blurb: Democratic senators asked the CFTC to restrict prediction market contracts on wildfires, warning that traders holding those positions could have a financial incentive to commit arson. The request adds to growing regulatory scrutiny of event-contract platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket, which have expanded into weather and disaster markets after federal courts cleared the way for election betting.

title: The billion-dollar question: How will the neolabs actually make money?
blurb: The author examines how neolabs, the new wave of AI-native research startups, will convert frontier models into durable revenue rather than perpetual burn. The piece argues that API access and per-token pricing alone won't cover training costs, pushing labs toward vertical applications, enterprise contracts, and infrastructure lock-in. For fintech operators building on top of these models, the unresolved question is who ultimately captures the margin as inference costs and pricing power shift.

title: Robinhood's Second Venture Fund Targets Y Combinator Startups in $200 Million IPO
blurb: Robinhood opened the order window for Robinhood Ventures Fund II, a $200M closed-end BDC that gives retail investors accreditation-free exposure to roughly 80 seed-stage Y Combinator startups, targeting an NYSE listing under RVII on Aug. 13. The vehicle pushes Robinhood's private-markets expansion into venture's riskiest tier, charging a 2% management fee plus 20% carry for total annual expenses near 4.18%.

title: BlackRock launches two tokenized money market funds for stablecoin reserves
blurb: BlackRock launched two tokenized money market products, BRSRV and a new onchain share class of its Select Treasury fund (BSTBL), both aimed at holding stablecoin reserves in cash, short-term Treasuries, and overnight repos. The launch extends the playbook behind its $2.6B BUIDL fund and puts BlackRock alongside Morgan Stanley, State Street, and Fidelity in courting stablecoin issuers looking to earn yield on reserves.

title: Crypto Card Volume Hits $748.7M in July, a Fifth Straight Monthly Gain: Paymentscan
blurb: Crypto payment card spending hit a record $748.7M in July, up 19.1% from June and 144.7% year-over-year, marking a fifth straight monthly all-time high as trading volumes sink to multi-year lows, per Paymentscan. RedotPay processed more than half the tracked volume at $395.1M, and cumulative card deposits crossed $10B around July 1, positioning stablecoin-funded cards as a direct bridge from onchain dollars to merchant payments.

title: The $114 Trillion Question: How DTCC Is Tokenizing the Entire U.S. Market
blurb: On July 15th, the DTCC ran a live production test that converted assets from its $114T custody base into digital tokens, traded them, and settled them back into conventional form without disrupting existing operations. The pilot signals the largest US clearing and settlement infrastructure is moving toward tokenized securities, which would pull on-chain settlement from fintech experiments into the core plumbing of American capital markets.

title: Kalshi CEO invokes Nasdaq, Uber and Airbnb in defense against New York lawsuit
blurb: Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour told CNBC that New York's $36B lawsuit alleging its event contracts are illegal gambling could be "copy and pasted" against Nasdaq, arguing the platform earns a 1% transaction fee on opposing user positions rather than booking bets against the house. The framing tests whether CFTC-regulated prediction markets can preempt state gambling law, a question that will shape how far sports-heavy event contracts can expand.

title: Robinhood is launching a publicly traded fund that invests in Y Combinator startups. Anyone can buy shares.
blurb: Robinhood Ventures Fund II will IPO on the NYSE under ticker RVII on August 12, offering 7.6 million shares at $25 each to give retail investors exposure to early and growth-stage Y Combinator startups. The closed-end structure applies the traditional 2-and-20 fee model to a retail product, following Fund I's March IPO that raised $315M and holds stakes in Databricks, Stripe, and Canva.

title: FalconX Cuts Staff on Extended Downturn in Crypto Markets
blurb: FalconX cut 10% of its global staff as the digital-asset brokerage braces for a prolonged crypto-market downturn, according to people familiar with the matter. The reduction at one of the largest institutional crypto brokers signals that trading-volume and prime-brokerage revenue have contracted enough to force cost cuts even at scaled players, a warning sign for the institutional-crypto infrastructure buildout.

title: Corgi On Pace to Launch 500 ETFs In First Year
blurb: Corgi is on pace to launch roughly 500 ETFs in its first year, already ranking among the largest US issuers by product count and exceeding what BlackRock accumulated over many years. The firm is targeting 1,000 funds spanning leveraged single stocks, buffered strategies, semiconductors and narrow themes, a volume-first playbook that pressures incumbents competing on brand and distribution rather than sheer product count.
